name: Virginia State Capitol
description: Neoclassical capitol building designed with Thomas Jefferson's input, completed in 1788; still houses the Virginia General Assembly.

name: Main Street Station
description: 1901 French Renaissance Revival railway station with a distinctive clock tower, in Shockoe Bottom; still an active Amtrak stop.

name: The Jefferson Hotel
description: Opulent 1895 Beaux-Arts hotel designed by Carrère and Hastings, known for its grand staircase and rooftop palm court.

name: Old City Hall
description: High Victorian Gothic government building completed in 1894, adjacent to Capitol Square; now used as office space.

name: Carpenter Theatre / Dominion Energy Center
description: 1928 Loew's movie palace restored as the Carpenter Theatre, now the anchor venue of the Dominion Energy Center for the Performing Arts.

name: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond
description: Aluminum-clad Fifth District Federal Reserve headquarters tower designed by Minoru Yamasaki, built 1975-1978 overlooking the James River.

name: James Monroe Building
description: State office tower on Capitol Square housing several Virginia state agencies, named for President James Monroe.

name: Dominion Energy tower (600 Canal Place)
description: High-rise corporate headquarters of Dominion Energy at 600 Canal Place, one of the tallest buildings in downtown Richmond's skyline.

name: Altria Theater
description: 1927 Shriners' Mosque-style auditorium later known as the Landmark Theater, now a major performing arts and concert venue near Monroe Park.

name: Byrd Theatre
description: Lavish 1928 movie palace on Cary Street with an original Wurlitzer organ, still operating as a single-screen cinema.

name: Monument Avenue streetscape
description: Grand tree-lined boulevard of Victorian and Beaux-Arts mansions with a landscaped median, a National Historic Landmark district.

name: Hollywood Cemetery
description: 1849 rural garden cemetery on the James River bluffs, burial site of two U.S. presidents and Confederate president Jefferson Davis.

name: Belle Isle footbridge
description: Pedestrian suspension footbridge beneath the Robert E. Lee Bridge connecting downtown to Belle Isle, a former factory site turned riverfront park.

name: Mayo Bridge
description: Richmond's oldest James River highway crossing, carrying US 360; the current structure dates to 1913 on a river-crossing site used since colonial times.

name: Canal Walk + Tredegar Iron Works
description: Riverfront walkway along the historic James River and Kanawha Canal, passing the ruins of the Tredegar Iron Works, a Confederate munitions foundry now home to the American Civil War Museum.

name: The Diamond
description: 1985 baseball stadium on North Arthur Ashe Boulevard, longtime home of the Richmond Flying Squirrels, now succeeded by a new ballpark under the CarMax Park name.

name: VCU Cabell Library
description: Main library of Virginia Commonwealth University's Monroe Park campus, named for novelist James Branch Cabell.

name: Maggie L. Walker memorial
description: Bronze statue of banker and civic leader Maggie L. Walker by sculptor Toby Mendez, dedicated 2017 at Broad and Adams streets in Jackson Ward.
